items.title: 'Nuclear power could triple by 2060'
items.summary: United Nations: The head of the UN nuclear agency said on Friday that he expects the use of nuclear power could more than triple by 2060.Rafael Grossi said in the International Atomic Energy Agency's annual report to the UN General Assembly that this will be driven by electrification, data centres powered by artificial intelligence and "technology companies' appetite for reliable, carbon-free power".Also read: Zelenskiy says Ukrainian, Russian and US negotiators to meet in early November in Abu DhabiNuclear energy is seen by a growing number of countries as key to improving their energy security, he said, stressing that it is on par with solar energy and "safer than every other option"."In 2025, more than 400 operating reactors in more than 30 countries produced 10 per cent of global electricity and a quarter of its low-carbon electricity," the IAEA director-general said. "More than 60 new reactors are under construction and the projections for future nuclear capacity have shifted dramatically upward."In addition to the growing use of nuclear energy for peaceful purposes, Grossi spoke about the nuclear programmes in Iran and North Korea, the "unprecedented threats to nuclear safety" from the war in Ukraine, and worrying reports that other countries he did not name are talking about acquiring nuclear weapons.On Iran, whose nuclear sites were struck by the US last year before the US and Israel launched a war on February 28, Grossi told UN member nations that the necessary technical work for a diplomatic agreement has been done."I call on the parties to redouble their efforts towards agreeing a diplomatic solution that includes the IAEA's indispensable verification role, without which no agreement can be sustainable," he said. "IAEA inspectors must be able to return to Iran expeditiously. That requires a return to the negotiating table."In North Korea, where leader Kim Jong Un has a growing nuclear programme without any IAEA oversight, Grossi warned that it "stands as a stark reminder of the consequences when red lines are crossed" in violation of UN Security Council resolutions banning nuclear weapons production.Also read: Melania Trump brokers Russia-Ukraine ceasefire in war-hit Oleshky, White House saysIn Ukraine, he singled out the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant, Europe's largest, saying it remains "in a precarious position" with frequent power losses, limited back-up diesel supplies "and military activity threatening the plant and the people who work there".On a positive note, Grossi said the IAEA has made "significant progress" in clarifying and resolving outstanding questions regarding Syria's nuclear activities after nearly two decades of uncertainty. That is as a result of engaging with the government of interim President Ahmad al-Sharaa, he said.He reported in September that the Bashar Assad-era government -- which was ousted in December 2024 by opposition forces led by al-Sharaa -- was constructing a nuclear reactor that was configured to produce fissile material for possible use in nuclear weapons.

items.title: Infosys CEO: Macro recovery ‘more uneven’
items.summary: Infosys had expected technology spending to recover in the second half of FY27, but the improvement is proving more uneven than anticipated, chief executive Salil Parekh said, as the IT services company cut its revenue growth guidance for the year.“We had a sense that the macro was settling down, so we had a guidance where the upper end looked at maybe things would settle down in the second half. Things are a little bit more uneven,” Parekh said during the post-results press conference.He added that technology spending could still stabilise over time, allowing the company to benefit if client budgets recover.Also Read: Infosys ADRs crash 6% after Q2 results as revenue guidance cut spooks investorsThe comments came as Infosys cut its FY27 revenue growth guidance in constant currency terms to 1-2% from 1.5-3% earlier, reflecting a more cautious view of the pace of recovery.Parekh said the revised guidance reflected what the company was seeing in the market rather than a precise prediction of when spending would improve.AI gains traction, but broad-based recovery remains elusiveWhile AI-related work is growing, the company is also seeing productivity gains from AI affect parts of its traditional services business as clients seek to lower costs.Parekh said the company had not quantified this compression but remained focused on growing AI-led revenue to offset the impact over time.Chief financial officer Jayesh Sanghrajka said AI-related revenue had risen to 8.2% of total revenue from 5.5% in the third quarter, with double-digit sequential growth over recent quarters.Parekh said the company saw a substantial long-term opportunity in AI services, with an addressable market of about $300 billion across six focus areas.However, the recovery remains uneven across industries. Parekh said Infosys was yet to see a pickup in retail, while communications remained another challenging segment.North America had also been softer over recent quarters, partly due to lower discretionary spending and client-specific ramp-downs, Sanghrajka said.Also Read: Infosys Q2 Results: Profit rises 6% YoY to Rs 7,823 crore; co lowers revenue guidanceThe company reported large deal wins worth $3.6 billion in the quarter, of which 61% was net new business. Sanghrajka said a major net-new deal would contribute minimally to FY27 revenue as it was expected to ramp up only towards the end of the fourth quarter, but could add more than 1% to revenue growth next year.Infosys retained its FY27 operating margin guidance of 20-22%.

items.summary: India’s business sentiment rebounded in the second quarter of this fiscal year, with the Business Confidence Index (BCI) rising to 107.8 from 99.8 in the April–June quarter, ending a four-quarter period of moderation driven by ongoing geopolitical tensions, according to the latest NCAER Business Expectations Survey.Conducted in September by the National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER), the survey sampled 502 companies across different sizes in six major cities: Delhi NCR in the north, Bengaluru and Chennai in the south, Kolkata in the east, and Mumbai and Pune in the west."Though BCI improved, it was lower than the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year (142.6 in 2025−26: Q2)," it said.Also read: India October business growth hits 4-month high; hiring stalls, PMI showsThe BCI evaluates four key parameters: expectations of improved macro-economic conditions over the next six months, expectations of better firm financial health over the next six months, a favorable current investment climate, and present capacity utilization at or near optimal levels.All four parameters recorded gains, driving the quarter-over-quarter uptick in business sentiment."The share of firms expecting 'overall economic conditions to improve in the next six months' increased from 43 per cent in 2026-27: Q1 to 50 per cent in 2026-27: Q2," NCAER said.Confidence regarding firm financial prospects over the coming six months expanded from 37% in Q1 to 41% in Q2. Similarly, positive assessments of the current investment climate grew from 26% to 30%. Opinions on optimal capacity utilization also saw an increase, climbing from 91% in the first quarter to 94% in the second.Segment-wise, the BCI for MSMEs moved up from 93 to 100, while for large enterprises it rose from 111.6 to 120.3.NCAER's Bornali Bhandari, who led the survey, said, "The data indicate a broad-based recovery in sentiments across both MSMEs and large firms"."Overall business prospects improved both domestically and externally, and cost sentiments have moderated," she added.

"IndiGo flights to and from Riyadh will remain cancelled until 31 October 2026 (inclusive), while flights to and from Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah will remain cancelled until 27 October 2026 (inclusive)," the mission said in a post on X.

Three schools in Delhi allegedly received bomb threat emails on Friday morning, prompting authorities to launch search operations, officials said.
No suspicious object has been found during searches so far, they said.
Sardar Patel Vidyalaya in Lodi Estate, Venkateshwar Global School in Rohini, and Salwan Public School in Mayur Vihar received the threat emails, following which authorities were informed.
Delhi Fire Service said teams rushed to the schools after receiving information about the threats, and the premises were evacuated as a precautionary measure.
Bomb disposal squads, dog squads, fire department and police personnel are conducting searches at the premises, officials said.
Investigation is underway to trace the source of the threat emails, they added.

items.title: No dilution in standards: NMC on denotification of medical education rules
items.summary:
The National Medical Commission has asserted that the de-notification of the Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations, 2023 will not dilute prescribed standards of medical education and are intended to remove overlapping procedures.
The Commission, which is the statutory body for medical education in the country, had on October 14 denotified the Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations (MSMER-2023).
The denotification "does not, in any manner, dilute the prescribed standards of medical education or the regulatory oversight exercised by NMC," a statement by the Commission said.
Under the National Medical Commission Act, 2019, the Undergraduate Medical Education Board (UGMEB) and Postgraduate Medical Education Board (PGMEB) are primarily entrusted with prescribing academic standards, minimum requirements and educational norms.
The Medical Assessment and Rating Board (MARB), under Section 26 of the Act is specifically empowered to assess and inspect .

items.title: Rupee rises 3 paise to 94.78 against US dollar during early trade
items.summary:
The rupee traded in a narrow range and edged up 3 paise to 94.78 against the US dollar in early trade on Friday amid elevated crude oil prices and foreign fund outflows.
Forex traders said rupee is under pressure amid persistent macroeconomic headwinds, including global dollar strength and Brent crude prices hovering near USD 113 per barrel.
At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 94.78, registering a gain of 3 paise over its previous close.
On Thursday, the rupee closed at 94.81 against the American currency.
Foreign investors turned cautious seeking safe-haven greenback assets amid elevated US Treasury yields,  said Anil Kumar Bhansali, Head of Treasury and Executive Director Finrex Treasury Advisors LLP.
Meanwhile, the dollar index, which gauges the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was trading at 101.64, higher by 0.04 per cent.
Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was trading higher by 0.42 per cent at USD 113.65 per barrel in .

Brook's 116-ball 202 propelled England to its fourth highest ODI score of 429-4 before it ran into Sri Lanka's super counterpunch to lose by two wickets.
Needing six runs off Josh Tongue's final two balls, Janith Liyanage lofted the fast bowler over long-off for a winning six to reach 430-8 and earn Sri Lanka their most memorable ODI victory since winning the 1996 World Cup.
Sri Lanka's astonishing run-chase was only second behind South Africa's 438-9 when it beat Australia by one wicket at Johannesburg in 2006.
"Incredible game of cricket, both teams were exceptional," Brook said. "Sri Lanka just outplayed us. They played exceptional cricket to knock off 400."

items.title: Asian Para Games: Sandeep, Haney clinch gold with world records for India
items.summary:
India's Sandeep and Haney won gold medals with world record performances in the men's 400m T64 and men's javelin throw F37/38 events respectively at the Asian Para Games here on Friday.
Sandeep clocked 52.28 seconds, a world record, to win the 400m T64 final at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium. He finished 0.85 seconds ahead of Saudi Arabia's Nour Alsana (53.13, season's best). Indian compatriot Ajay Kumar took bronze in 53.61, a Games Record, while China's Huang Ruihua was fourth with a personal best of 54.39.
In the javelin throw F37/38 final at the same venue, Haney produced a world record throw of 60.49m for gold, scoring 1116 Raza points. Iran's Hormoz Seidikazpounji took silver with a personal best of 50.68m (1009 points), while China's Yu Chengjie claimed bronze with an Asian record 53.66m (943 points).
India have thus reached 100 medals in total in this edition of the sporting extravaganza.

FIFA opens bidding for 2030 & 2034 World Cup
items.summary: FIFA opened the bidding process for US media rights to the 2030 World Cup on Thursday along with an option to secure the 2034 edition, adding that it has yet to decide whether to keep the controversial hydration breaks introduced this year that opened up additional advertising windows ​for broadcasters.FIFA said in a press release that it was open to "innovative approaches" to reach large audiences and that the bid submission deadline is November 19.Fox held the exclusive English-language FIFA broadcast rights in the United States for the last three World Cups, including the 2026 edition that was co-hosted by the US, Canada and Mexico, while Telemundo held the Spanish language rights during that same time.Spain, which won the 2026 World Cup, will co-host the 2030 edition with Portugal and ‌Morocco, ⁠although Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay will also stage matches to mark the tournament's 100th anniversary. Saudi Arabia will host the 2034 World Cup.FIFA Chief Business Officer Romy Gai, speaking to reporters after the announcement, said world soccer's governing body is still evaluating whether to keep the hydration breaks that were put in place for the 2026 World Cup to help players cope with high temperatures but also proved lucrative for broadcasters.The hydration breaks fuelled debate over their impact on the game, with some viewers complaining ​about being exposed to commercials during the three-minute stoppages in each half."If the average temperature will be higher than the normal average is in these countries we expect to confirm having the hydration break, but not automatically," said Gai."It's not the final decision because this is something that we need to further engage with all the stakeholders."According to FIFA, the 2026 World Cup averaged 13.5 million viewers per match on linear and streaming platforms in the United States, up 166% on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.Earlier this week, Netflix announced that it secured the rights to broadcast the 2030 World Cup ​in Spain and Andorra.The Saudi climate will likely force FIFA to hold the 2034 tournament in the Northern Hemisphere winter, just like it did for the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, but Gai said that while it is a possibility the matter has not yet been discussed officially."It's too early for that. But this is something that we are concretely considering," Gai said when asked about staging the 2034 World Cup in November-December of that year instead of the tournament's traditional June-July slot."It will be further assessed and we will share the same comments with any bidders when it will be the time to sit down and analyze how it can be to play the World Cup in 2034. It is a clear possibility ... but it's not yet confirmed. So we need to understand more."

items.title: US proposes rule to crack down on high-tech investments in China, others
items.summary:
The US Treasury Department proposed a rule on Thursday to crack down on American high-tech investments such as supercomputing and artificial intelligence in China, Russia, North Korea and other "countries of concern".
The US government has been working for years to deny China and other adversaries investments that could help them boost their military power.
That programme began in 2023 when then-President Joe Biden signed an executive order putting restrictions on outbound US investments in sectors such as semiconductors, quantum computing and artificial intelligence going into China. Treasury later established the Outbound Investment Security Programme.
In December 2025, Congress passed a law that codified and expanded the programme to target more technologies and more foreign countries, including Cuba, Iran, North Korea and Russia.

items.summary:
A magnitude 7 earthquake hit China's Tibet region on Thursday evening, killing at least 16 people, injuring 46 and collapsing hundreds of homes in the northern regional city of Nagqu, official media said.
Search and rescue efforts continued following the collapse of at least 339 homes and 20 livestock sheds, the Nagqu media office said, citing city government officials. Among the injured, 11 people were in serious condition and the other 35 sustained minor injuries, the media office said.
More than 1,600 people from the local county were deployed for rescue efforts. Supplies including 1,000 prefabricated housing units, around 3,000 tents and folding beds, as well as flashlights and winter clothing arrived in the region.
China's official news agency Xinhua said on Friday that communication in part of the region has been down. Local railway authorities have taken emergency actions to halt trains passing through the region.

items.title: 2,700 detained amid riots & looting in France
items.summary: French police have taken 2,700 people into custody since Saturday in connection with riots and looting, Reuters reported citing Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin, as authorities brace for further unrest across the country."Some 2,700 people have been taken into police custody since Saturday in connection with these riots and looting," Darmanin said in an interview with French news channel LCI.French President Emmanuel Macron said on Thursday that "illegitimate" protests would be prohibited in the coming days. He blamed "seditious" ultra-left groups and vandals for last weekend's riots and looting.Speaking after a meeting with intelligence chiefs and senior ministers, Macron said demonstrations organised by groups such as trade unions would be permitted, although authorities could divert them to alternative routes to protect businesses."Last Saturday we had political and seditious acts by ultra-left groups whose aim is to bring down the Republic," he said.His remarks came as authorities across France prepared for fresh protests following some of the country's worst urban unrest in years.Darmanin said he wanted voting rights to be suspended for people who violate bans on demonstrations. He also called for restrictions on social media access for those involved in violence, looting or attacks on police.Authorities have banned all protests scheduled for Saturday in Marseille and Lyon, France's second- and third-largest cities. However, new demonstrations are already being planned ahead of a weekend that officials fear could turn volatile.France's main student union, UNEF, has called for rallies on Saturday, while the Yellow Vest movement, an anti-establishment force that emerged in 2018, has submitted plans for a march through central Paris.Businesses in central Paris have started boarding up their shop windows in anticipation of possible violence. Luxury goods group Hermes said it had strengthened security at its stores across France.Organisers of Art Basel Paris, an international art collectors fair being held in an exhibition hall in central Paris, said the event would remain closed throughout the weekend.In the northern city of Orleans, authorities were preparing for possible unrest as the far-right National Rally prepared to hold its annual meeting, while unions and left-wing groups planned demonstrations.A student protest scheduled for Thursday in Paris was initially banned but was later permitted to proceed. However, transit authorities shut metro stations in central Paris in anticipation of unauthorised gatherings.PUBLIC ANGERFrance was shaken by violence on the fringes of nationwide protests on October 17, exposing the extent of public anger and raising concerns about the ability of security services to maintain order.Two people have been arrested in connection with an arson attack on the city hall in Limoges, according to French officials and media reports.A third consecutive night of local curfews passed without major incidents in areas affected by the violence, giving the government some respite ahead of the weekend.The unrest has also exposed deeper discontent in France, where rising energy costs, mounting pressure on household budgets and concerns about deteriorating public services have fuelled frustration among workers and younger people.France's political class has meanwhile become embroiled in a bitter blame game, with the government accusing far-left political groups of fuelling the unrest.(With inputs from Reuters)

items.title: 7.0 earthquake in Tibet kills at least 16
items.summary: Beijing: A strong earthquake killed at least 16 people and injured 46 in China's remote Tibet region, state media said, citing local authorities.More than 300 houses collapsed in the 7.0 magnitude quake, which struck on Thursday at 10:33 pm (1433 GMT).Officials were still evaluating the damage, and disaster relief work was ongoing, state news agency Xinhua said.China Central Television (CCTV) put the number of injured at 46, 11 of them seriously, with 339 houses collapsed or damaged, citing local officials.Videos posted by CCTV showed workers running out of restaurants and objects falling off shelves at supermarkets when the quake struck.The epicentre was located in a mountainous area about 190 kilometres (120 miles) east-northeast of Nagqu, and 390 kilometres northeast of the regional capital Lhasa, the US Geological Survey said.It struck at a shallow depth of around 10 kilometres.A level-III earthquake disaster emergency response was activated in the area, CCTV reported.The epicentre was in Maru township in Baqen county. Township deputy head Lhawang Dagpo said the quake was clearly felt at the township office, which sustained cracks in the walls, according to Xinhua.Power and telecoms services were disrupted in the county seat, the agency said.More than 300 police officers have been dispatched for relief work while the regional fire and rescue corps has mobilised 347 personnel to the affected areas, Xinhua reported.Rescue workers clambered through damaged buildings, some with collapsed roofs, and carrying one person, footage on CCTV showed.It also showed rescue workers shining flashlights on other damaged buildings and soldiers lining up ready to be deployed.Earthquakes in China are relatively common.In January 2025, at least 126 people were killed in an earthquake in Tibet's rural Tingri county.In December 2023, a quake in remote Gansu province in northwest China killed at least 127 people, according to state media.That quake was China's deadliest since 2014, when more than 600 people died in the southwestern province of Yunnan.A huge tremor in 2008 in Sichuan province left some 90,000 people dead or missing, including around 5,000 schoolchildren.

items.title: ITBP DG gives a peek into troops' LAC plan
items.summary: New Delhi: The ITBP has raised drone platoons in all its border units, prepared a new 'Strike' course to better handle Galwan-like battles and is creating underground infrastructure along the front "in a big way" as part of the new warfare to counter India's "biggest adversary" China, the force's chief said on Thursday.ITBP Director General (DG) Shatrujeet Singh Kapoor told his troops at a force base in Rajasthan's Alwar that countering China through "traditional" means of warfare was a thing of the past and hence they were investing in modernizing the force, its weapons, vehicles and border posts.The Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), raised in 1962, guards the 3,488-km-long Line of Actual Control (LAC) with China.The DG noted that the recent Ukraine-Russia and Iran-US wars have shown the importance of drone and anti-drone technology through which a small country can overwhelm a bigger nation during conflict.Also read | Army invites applications for 75-day internship programme in defence technologiesKapoor, who is set to retire from service on October 31, addressed his troops during an investiture ceremony held leading up to the force's 65th Raising Day on October 24.He said the China front was our "most difficult" border, and China was a "powerful" neighbour and India's "biggest adversary," requiring enhanced capabilities to "counter" it."Drones have become a major challenge and an opportunity also. It will be difficult to compete with China using traditional methods... They have modernised and invested heavily in their PLA but drones are such that a small country can give a befitting contest to a bigger nation," he said.He noted that almost 10,000-15,000 Russian troops are killed in the war with Ukraine every month."This is despite the fact that it (Russia) is a big country and a superpower. They (Russia) thought that they would capture (Ukraine) in 1-2 months but it is the fourth year counting, and every month they (Russians) have 10-15 thousand bodies reaching them," the DG said.He added that this caused such "big damage" and that Russia was suffering because of that one decision.Kapoor then cited the Iran-US war as an example, noting that Iran, without an Air Force, Navy, or Army, engaged in combat with the global superpower.Also read | From 290-km BrahMos to a proposed 1,500-km variant: How Operation Sindoor boosted India's missile profile"The role of traditional armies has changed since the drones arrived, and we must embrace drone and anti-drone systems in a big way," he said.Kapoor said the approximately 95,000-personnel-strong, mountain-warfare-trained ITBP has received government funds worth Rs 400 crore and 70 per cent of these funds have been earmarked for enhancing the force's drone warfare capabilities."Each border guarding battalion now has a drone platoon, and we are training drone pilots and building drones too.""The Ministry of Home Affairs has also granted in-principle approval to a bigger modernisation scheme of Rs 4,000 crore, of which we will earmark Rs 1,000 crore for drone and anti-drone systems," the DG said.He informed the troops that a new course named 'Strike' has been developed to train ITBP personnel, which will enhance their capabilities to face Galwan-like situations. The entire force will undergo this training by the end of 2027.Chinese soldiers used stones, nail-studded sticks, iron rods and clubs while carrying out brutal attacks on Indian soldiers along the LAC at Galwan (Ladakh) in June, 2020 resulting in 20 casualties on the Indian side while China belatedly claimed only 4 of its troops were killed. Multiple reports suggested that the Chinese fatalities were much higher.The ITBP chief added that a new combat team, the Shaurya commandos, has been raised. This team displayed its skills during the "ongoing" faceoff with the Chinese PLA troops at multiple places in Arunachal Pradesh.These commandos will be in every border battalion and will give the force a distinct identity, he said.The DG said the force was constructing underground shelters (bunkers) at border locations "in a big way," learning from the lessons of the new warfare, as above-ground buildings can become a target in 'hot war' situations, indicating the post-Operation Sindoor conflict with Pakistan.He said a pilot project is underway in this context and they plan to have these under-ground shelters in the coming years, equipped with the same comfort available in above-ground buildings.Kapoor said the force also worked on the ensuring the comfort and operational prepardeness of the troops by insulating 342 out of 383 barracks present in areas which face "sub-zero" temperatures, has procured 141 generator sets to ensure electricity at remote troop locations and got solar water heaters installed at a number of such facilities."This will help enhance the morale and confidence of the troops and improve the ITBP's operational preparedness," he said.The DG added that a 'cold start kit' was provided to border units which helps vehicles get immediate ignition in icy weather."Many years ago when we were in Kosovo in sub zero temperatures the vehicles there used to start in one crank. We wondered why this wasn't happening here? We did some experiments and now we can do it," he said.The DG also asked his troops to keep fit and healthy, saying a new diet plan has been introduced in the force and the "very high" content of sugar and oil has been lessened.He expressed concern over the cases of Alcohol Dependence Syndrome (ADS) in the ITBP which have doubled or tripled since 2020.The DG also asked the troops to be cautious against ADS and 'honey trap' instances of being lured by someone into sharing sensitive information through the social media.He added that the ITBP was also modernising its weapons, some of which are about 50 years old, and improving mobility through the procurement of new all-terrain Vehicles, ground vehicles and quick reaction vehicles,We have prepared a plan to become a specialised high-altitude mountain fighting force through all these measures, Kapoor said.

items.title: Wall Street dumps AI for Buffett’s Berkshire
items.summary: For three weeks, Wall Street sold one of the market’s hottest trades and bought one of its oldest. Chip stocks fell about 15 per cent. Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway rose about 7 per cent.Between October 2 and October 20, the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) lost 15.1 per cent, while Berkshire’s Class B shares (BRK-B) gained 7.4 per cent, according to Yahoo Finance.On Tuesday, BRK-B closed at a record high for the first time since May 2, 2025, the day before Buffett said Greg Abel would take over as CEO.On Wednesday, both the Class B and Class A (BRK-A) shares touched new intraday records.Berkshire hits a record as chip stocks slump 15%: the rare dot-com-era signal investors are watching, and what it may mean for your portfolioThe wait was long. In those 17 months, the S&P 500 gained more than 35 per cent, and Berkshire only now got back to a record close.The recent moves have been strikingly one-sided. From October 6 to Tuesday, SOXX fell in 10 of 11 sessions, and Berkshire rose on nine of those days.On the chip sector’s two worst days, October 14 and October 16, Berkshire posted two of its best gains of the run. Since October 1, the stock has mostly gone up on days when chips went down.For now, that makes Berkshire look like a hedge against the AI chip trade.Berkshire is on track to rise in 14 of its last 15 sessions. It also strung together a 10-day winning streak, its first since 2018.The gap between the two is historic too. Over the 12 sessions from October 2 through Tuesday, Berkshire beat SOXX by 22 percentage points.Yahoo Finance compared Berkshire with the PHLX Semiconductor Index going back to 1994, and found this is the widest 12-session gap since early 2010. The all-time record, set in April 2000, was close to 40 points.The gap alone is not the rarest part. The combination is. Chips fell at least 14 per cent while Berkshire gained at least 7 per cent over 12 sessions. Before this month, that last happened on October 3, 2001. Every earlier case came in 1995-96 or in 2000-01, when the dot-com bubble was bursting.History gives a mixed message from here. In the short term, chips bounced back. They were higher a week later in five of the six earlier cases, and they are rebounding on Wednesday as well. A year later, the picture was weaker: chips were lower in five of six cases, and the S&P 500 fell in four.Under Abel, Berkshire is also using its cash differently. It bought back about $4.5 billion of its own stock in the second quarter. That ended 14 straight quarters in which it sold more of its own stock than it bought, and its cash pile has come down from a record $397 billion.Buffett said on September 18 that he would step down as chairman too. The stock hit its low about two weeks later.The tech bets are changing as well. A few years ago, Apple made up nearly 45 per cent of Berkshire’s invested assets. Buffett was never known as a tech investor. What drew him to Apple was customer loyalty and people’s willingness to pay premium prices for iPhones, Macs and iPads, not the technology itself.In just a few months, Alphabet has become for Abel what Apple was for Buffett. Google handled roughly 90 per cent of global internet search traffic in September, which is part of the appeal. But the AI ambitions are what interest both men most. Since Alphabet added generative AI and large language models to Google Cloud, the world’s third-largest cloud platform, sales in that high-margin business have grown very fast.Abel is also looking beyond Alphabet. An October 14 filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission shows Berkshire is buying 10 million shares of Bending Spoons in a private placement at $33 a share, an investment of $330 million. It follows a $600 million investment at the company’s IPO in July.The company’s model has some similarity to Berkshire’s own. Berkshire grew to a $1 trillion market value by buying about five dozen companies, and pieces of others, and usually holding them for a long time.Bending Spoons, based in Italy, buys technology platforms and uses software, AI, price hikes and layoffs to make them leaner and to sell more subscriptions. So far it has bought AOL, Vimeo, Brightcove, Eventbrite and WeTransfer, among others. The company is already profitable and growing quickly.The next test comes with Berkshire’s third-quarter results, expected on Saturday, November 7.

items.title: Gold hits 2-month low as Silver prices slide
items.summary: Gold rate today fell to its lowest level since August 4. Spot gold slid 1.9 per cent to $4,060.37 per ounce to its lowest level in more than two months on Thursday. US gold futures for December delivery fell 1.8 per cent to $4,075.70 per ounce. This comes as a rally in oil prices heightened inflation worries ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy decision next week.Spot silver dropped 3.9 per cent to $55.7225 per ounce, platinum slid 2.9 per cent to $1,581.73, its lowest since July 29, while palladium fell 2.5 per cent to $1,059.75 after hitting its lowest level since June 2025.Gold Rate Prediction"Gold prices can fall further... because we are still seeing a lot of uncertainty around the energy market," said Soni Kumari, analyst at ANZ.135100704Brent prices rose to their highest since May after more Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concerns over a broader escalation of conflict and further disruptions to crude oil supplies from the world's key exporting region.Meanwhile, US consumer and producer inflation data came in hotter than expected last week, largely on higher energy costs. That strengthens the case for tighter policy, even though Fed officials are still expected to hold off when they meet on October 27-28.While gold is typically considered a hedge against inflation, higher interest rates reduce the appeal of the non-yielding asset.Goldman Sachs expects one more 25-basis-point hike in December, lifting the peak policy rate range to 4.00 per cent-4.25 per cent. Traders are pricing in an 86 per cent likelihood of a December increase, according to CME's FedWatch Tool.135094387US Personal Consumption Expenditures data, set for release on October 29 and closely watched by the central bank, could give more clues on rate outlook."Given that the PCE data will show that prices rose at an uncomfortably high pace for the Fed, the FOMC communications may strike a hawkish tone and that could weigh on gold prices," said Hamad Hussain, climate and commodities economist at Capital Economics.

items.title: US visitor visa wait hits 12 months in India
items.summary: Indian applicants seeking US business and tourist visas may have to wait up to 12 months for the next available interview appointment in Mumbai. Hyderabad follows with a 10.5-month wait, while New Delhi has an estimated wait of 11 months, according to the department’s Global Visa Wait Times update dated October 21.Kolkata applicants face an estimated 8.5-month wait for the next available appointment, while Chennai has a 7.5-month wait. Mumbai also records the highest average wait time among the five cities at 12.5 months, measured from visa fee payment to the interview date in the previous month.Also Read: Australia’s new arrival control law raises questions for students and workers returning homeThe waiting period varies considerably by visa category. Applicants seeking student and exchange visitor visas generally face shorter queues, while appointment availability for petition-based work visas differs across consular posts.City-wise US visa appointment wait timesIndian cityVisitor visa (B1/B2): Average waitNext available visitor visa slotStudent/exchange visa (F, M, J)Petition-based work visa (H, L, O, P, Q)Mumbai12.5 months12 months4 months2 monthsHyderabad10.5 months10.5 months1 month6.5 monthsNew Delhi7 months11 months3 months3.5 monthsKolkata8.5 months8.5 months2.5 months1 monthChennai7.5 months7.5 months3.5 months2.5 monthsSource: US Department of State, Global Visa Wait Times, updated October 21, 2026.Student visa slots available soonerThe data shows that applicants seeking F, M and J visas, which cover student and exchange visitor categories, generally face shorter waits than visitor visa applicants.Also Read: Norway named best among National Geographic's world travel map for 2027; Indian city among the topHyderabad has the shortest estimated wait in this category at one month, followed by Kolkata at 2.5 months. New Delhi applicants face a three-month wait, while Chennai and Mumbai have estimated waits of 3.5 months and four months, respectively.For petition-based visas, including H, L, O, P and Q categories, Kolkata has the shortest estimated wait at one month. Mumbai follows at two months, while Chennai and New Delhi have waits of 2.5 months and 3.5 months, respectively. Hyderabad has the longest wait in this category at 6.5 months.The figures cover grouped visa categories and should not be interpreted as separate estimates for individual classifications such as H-1B or L-1 visas.Although, the state department cautions that these estimates do not guarantee an appointment within a specified period. items.title: SpaceX-Tesla merger: How to tackle China risk
items.summary: Elon Musk's potential mega-merger of Tesla and SpaceX would likely face a China-shaped hurdle from regulators on both sides of the Pacific over concerns about national security and the sharing of data and technology.The world's richest person said on Tuesday his two companies had set up special committees to discuss a union, calling a merger a "good idea". Turning it into reality, however, would mean navigating the thorny issue of Tesla's heavy reliance on China for manufacturing versus SpaceX's defence business.Rocket company SpaceX is increasingly reliant on sensitive US government and defence contracts, which could subject any merger involving Tesla's business in China to intense scrutiny on national security grounds.Also read: What to know about the Ebola outbreak that has spread from Congo to 4 other countriesChinese regulators also require Tesla to keep confidential user data collected by its automated driving systems firmly in China, and any firewall would have to prevent the flow of information or technology in either direction.Below are some ways that Musk and the companies could look to clear any barriers put up by Washington or Beijing.Could Tesla keep its China business?One potential option would be for the merged company to create a firewall around Tesla's Chinese operations to block access to sensitive data from SpaceX and other parts of the business. Such a move is not unheard of, said Daniel Kollar, head of automotive and mobility practice at consultancy Intralink Group.Plenty of companies have been able to run major defence businesses outside of China while maintaining operations in the country, he said, citing Airbus and Honeywell.Also read: Beyond the ballot: Why Israel's next leader may stick to Netanyahu's doctrineSpaceX's defence-related businesses include Starshield, which develops military and intelligence satellite systems for the Pentagon.A two-way firewall would also likely be the minimum requirement to ensure Tesla's data from Chinese drivers stays in China, analysts said. Since 2021, Tesla has been complying with Beijing's requirement to keep all driver data inside of China.Tesla could continue to operate in China for years to come as a self-contained unit with its own research and development and strict agreements to keep all data inside China, said Michael Dunne, CEO of automotive advisory firm Dunne Insights, which closely follows China's auto industry.Keeping both Beijing and Washington happy about such a firewall, however, could be tricky, said Christopher Tang, a professor at UCLA's Anderson School of Management who specializes in ​global supply chains. He said the Chinese government is likely to try to use any proposed merger to negotiate a range of items as a condition for approval."China will use it as leverage," Tang said. "They have the bargaining power right now."Ioannis Kokkoris, professor of competition law and economics at Queen Mary University of London, identified two possible concessions that China could seek: access for Chinese companies to strategically significant technologies, and commitments to retain manufacturing capacity and investment in China.Any demand to share sensitive SpaceX-related technology, however, would run directly into US security restrictions.What about divestment?Analysts have said there were likely three broad paths towards divestment: a spinoff in which Tesla retains a majority economic interest, a sale paired with long-term brand licensing agreements, or an outright sale, possibly to another automaker.Any kind of divestment would come with plenty of complications, including the looming question of who would buy the asset. China's automakers, which do not need any extra capacity, are unlikely to be interested, said Li Yanwei, an analyst at the China Automobile Dealers Association.Many foreign automakers, on the other hand, are already strapped for cash, making them unlikely buyers as well. Kollar said Musk would be more likely to sell the China operation off for parts rather than hand control to anyone else.But Kollar added that unless Musk wanted to signal a retreat from the auto business, he expected Tesla to find a way to retain its China operations under the existing ownership structure.Tesla China and China's State Administration of Market Regulation did not reply to requests for comment.China still needed for cash flowA clean break from China could be difficult. Chinese suppliers are deeply integrated in Musk's broader empire and Tesla's Shanghai production accounted for more than 50% of its global output, according to Yale Zhang, managing director at Shanghai-based consultancy AutoForesight.Some investors, though, say those considerations aren't big enough to get in the way of a deal.Brian Mulberry, chief market strategist at Zacks Investment Management, a Tesla and SpaceX investor, said Tesla's China manufacturing base is considerable, but the electric vehicle maker has already been making moves to expand US production, particularly for humanoid robots and the Cybercab driverless car, and many investors are more focused on Musk's promises for where these are headed.Mulberry also said he thinks Tesla would argue to US regulators that its China operations wouldn't overlap with SpaceX, but if unsuccessful, he thinks Tesla could shut or scale back its China production."It's short-term enough and small enough to be digestible," he said.Tang, the UCLA professor, said that while Tesla's future prospects may lie outside of China, its current EV business is heavily reliant on it. Much of the cash needed to finance its future bets comes from China EV production, he said."That is exactly why China will take advantage of this moment," Tang said. "Because you still need them."

items.title: Crime Branch summons CJP's Saurav, Ashutosh
items.summary: New Delhi: Delhi Police Crime Branch has summoned Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka to its Rajouri Garden office on Thursday.The development comes a day after a Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) court ordered their release from judicial custody after accepting their personal and surety bonds and taking written undertakings from them to maintain peace and abide by the law.SEM Ritu Raj directed the two leaders to furnish personal and surety bonds of Rs 50,000 each until the conclusion of the enquiry. The court also directed them to appear on every hearing date and comply with the conditions specified in their bonds and undertakings.Also read: INDIA bloc leaders to hold online meeting on Thursday, roadmap for 'vote chori' protests on agendaIn their written undertakings, Das and Ranka promised not to breach peace or disturb public tranquillity. They also undertook not to call for protests at Jantar Mantar until the site is denotified in accordance with the law, and said any future protests would be conducted within the constitutional framework."Further judicial custody does not appear to be necessary at this stage, particularly after written undertakings before this Court," the SEM court observed while ordering their release.The court directed the investigating officer to submit a verification report regarding the sureties at the next hearing. The matter has been listed for further proceedings on October 23 at 3 pm, with the two leaders and their sureties directed to remain present.Earlier, Delhi Police had sought a further three-day extension of their judicial custody, arguing that the apprehension of a breach of peace and law and order persisted. Police also cited alleged differences between statements made by the leaders before the court and their subsequent remarks to the media.Also read:'Will not take down Indian Flag': Priyanka Gandhi's son alleges 'protest' photos pulled down at Bikaner House exhibitionDuring the hearing, counsel for the two leaders tendered an unconditional apology to the court over the conduct cited by the police and assured that it would not be repeated.Das and Ranka were detained in connection with an October 13 protest at Jantar Mantar, which had been denotified as a designated protest site. The police had alleged that they entered the area through private premises and violated conditions relating to maintaining peace.The SEM court has clarified that the enquiry in the matter will continue in accordance with the law.

items.title: Ahmedabad set to host first Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship from Oct 23
items.summary:
Ahmedabad will host the inaugural Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship from October 23 to 31, bringing together 13 nations for nine days of the competition.
Organised by the Amateur Kabaddi Federation of India (AKFI) with the approval of the International Kabaddi Federation (IKF), the championship will feature 23 squads and more than 400 athletes competing in 62 matches.
The championship was formally unveiled at a curtain-raiser event on Wednesday.
The Indian men's team will be captained by Surjeet Singh, while Nidhi Sharma will lead the women's team.
The participating nations are India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Nigeria, Kenya, Tanzania, Canada, Singapore, Malaysia, Uganda, England, Scotland, and Australia.
The semifinals in both categories will take place on October 30, followed by the finals on October 31.
"It is a proud moment for Indian kabaddi to host the first Commonwealth Championship in Ahmedabad," said AKFI secretary Jitendra Pran Singh Thakur in a statement.

Dawood Ibrahim is in Pakistan: India at UN
items.summary: New York: India on Wednesday (local time) strongly hit out at the UN rapporteurs for bias in a counter-terror report and called for high standards of impartiality.UN rapporteur Ben Saul in his report had described Dawood Ibrahim as the leader of the "India-based" D-Company criminal gang with terrorist ties.Taking umbrage at this, Indian diplomat Raghoo Puri told the UN Assembly, "We express serious concern at the unacceptable situation of the SR releasing reports with factual inaccuracies, while not being held accountable for them. This presents Member States with a fait accompli, which is unfortunate for this organization that is facing challenges of legitimacy."Also read: India urges orderly, time-bound transition for UN mechanism continuing work of tribunals on genocide, war crimesPuri underlined that Dawood was a wanted criminal and was based in Pakistan, a country in which Osama bin Laden had been found and neutralized.#WATCH | New York | While participating in the interactive Dialogue with Special Rapporteur, First Secretary Raghoo Puri says, "...My delegation has been pointing out in other forums as well our serious concern about the unacceptable situation of the SR (Special Rapporteur) releasing reports with factual inaccuracies while not being held accountable for them. This presents member states with a fait accompli, which is unfortunate for this organization that is facing challenges of legitimacy... The report mentions that in 2003, the Security Council listed the leader of one criminal group, D-Company, for association with Al-Qaeda... This organization and its listed leader, Dawood Ibrahim, have been wanted in India for terror attacks since 1993. This is clearly written in the narrative summary of reasons for listing under the 1267 sanctions regime. Not mentioning this fact is regrettable, and such incompetence on the part of special mandate holders does this organization tremendous harm... To date, he remains a wanted criminal in my country and, as per the UN's listing entry, resides in the same country where Osama bin Laden was found and neutralized... We also note the clear bias in different parts of the report and also note with concern certain media allegations against this important office. We would urge that the highest standards of probity and impartiality be maintained..."He adds, "It seems to have become fashionable for sponsors of terror to use human rights and the framework of counter-terrorism to justify their misdeeds... Regarding the statement just made by the delegate of Pakistan, everyone in this room knows that what has been mentioned against my country, including about the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, is pure propaganda made for very narrow political gains. These have been made by the actual rulers of Pakistan, which is its military... J&K and Ladakh are an inalienable part of India and have been so and will always remain. I would not like to dignify the statement by the Pakistani delegate with any further comment."(Source: X/Permanent Mission of India to the United Nations, New York)— ANI (@ANI) October 22, 2026"The report mentions that in 2003, the Security Council listed the leader of one criminal group, D-Company, for association with Al-Qaeda. Read in isolation, this line paints a very different picture from the actual reality. This organization and its listed leader, Dawood Ibrahim, has been wanted in India for terror attacks since 1993. This is clearly written in the narrative summary of reasons of listing under the 1267 sanctions regime. Not mentioning this fact is regrettable, and such incompetent- incompetence on part of special mandate holders does this organization tremendous harm. Let me correct it for the record. This individual fled India much before the 2003 listing, and it was during this period, from outside our country, that he was listed for being associated with Al-Qaeda and with Osama bin Laden. To date, he remains a wanted criminal in my country, and as per the UN's listing entry, resides in the same country where Osama bin Laden was found and neutralized," the Indian diplomat said.India also hit out at the bias in the report saying that human right framework can't judge perpetrators of terror."It seems to have become fashionable for sponsors of terror to use human rights and the framework of counterterrorism to justify their misdeeds. Human rights framework cannot be the refuge of the perpetrators of terror and those who propagate radicalization and extremism. Terrorism can never be justified," he said.Puri also hit out at a remark made by the Pakistdelegation, reaffirming that Jammu and Kashmir were integral parts of India."Regarding the statement just made by the delegate of Pakistan, everyone in this room knows that what has been mentioned against my country, including about the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, is pure propaganda made for very narrow political gains. And these have been on account of the actual rulers of Pakistan, which is its military. I would like to reiterate for the record that Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh are an inalienable part of India, and have been so, and will always remain. I would not like to dignify the statement of- by the Pakistani delegate with any further comment," he said.On Tuesday, India had asserted that human rights should not be used as an instrument of political pressure or selective country targeting, while calling for accountability, transparency and cooperation to address enforced disappearances at the United Nations General Assembly's Third Committee.Delivering India's statement on the agenda item concerning the Working Group on Enforced or Involuntary Disappearances, Ministry of External Affairs Deputy Secretary Barkha Tamrakar highlighted the constitutional and institutional safeguards available in India to address allegations of human rights violations.

items.summary:
The Trump administration moved on Wednesday to end its legal fight to overhaul a popular student loan forgiveness programme.
The Department of Justice appealed after federal judges ruled in June in favour of advocates who said the Public Service Loan Forgiveness programme risked becoming a tool for political retribution. Federal officials provided no explanation, but advocates praised the ruling.

items.title: Suvarna Raj bags gold in women's discus throw
items.summary: Aichi-Nagoya: India's Suvarna Raj won the gold medal in the women's discus throw F54 event at the Asian Para Games 2026 with a best effort of 15.66 metres, securing the country's first gold medal of the day on Thursday.Competing in a six-athlete field, Suvarna delivered a consistent performance, recording four throws beyond the 15-metre mark across her six attempts.Her gold-medal-winning effort came in her fifth attempt, helping her finish at the top of the podium and add another gold to India's medal tally at the continental para-sporting event.Iran's Shahla Hadidi secured the silver medal with a best throw of 15.45 metres, while Vietnam's Nguyen Thi Ngoc Thuy claimed bronze with an effort of 14.65 metres.Suvarna's victory marked a strong start to the day for the Indian contingent as the country's athletes continued their campaign at the Asian Para Games. Her medal marked India's 15th gold at the Games.Meanwhile, Indian para-shuttlers Manisha Ramadass and Pramod Bhagat settled for the bronze medal in the mixed doubles SL3-SU5 event after losing their semifinal against Indonesia's Oktila LeRatri and Hikmat Ramdani.The Indian pair went down 21-16, 13-21, 17-21 in a three-game contest, conceding the match after winning the opening game.Ratri and Ramdani will now face India's Thulasimathi Murugesan and Nitesh Kumar in the final, setting up an opportunity for India to secure the gold medal in the event.Earlier today, Indian para-archer Swati Chaudhary won the silver medal in the women's W1 individual archery event after losing to China's Mengkan Cen 4-6.Swati had a chance to win India's first gold medal in archery at the ongoing edition, taking a 4-2 lead after three ends. However, Cen staged a comeback to win the final 6-4, leaving the Indian archer with the silver medal.With the three medals won so far in the day, India's medal tally now stands at 65 medals with 15 gold medals, 22 silver medals and 28 bronze medals.

items.title: Car registrations plunge 22% this Navratri
items.summary: Mumbai: Even as carmakers said deliveries this Navratri were robust, car registrations declined sharply, according to provisional data from the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA). Passenger vehicle registrations fell 21.9% to 1.83 lakh units between October 11 and 20, the steepest drop among all vehicle categories.The fall largely reflects a high base. Last year's Navratri coincided with the rollout of GST 2.0, after sales had come to a standstill for half of August and almost all of September. This year, momentum continued even through Shradh, a period considered inauspicious.Also Read: Navratri shoppers splurge on clothes, appliances as gadgets get pricier"The dip is largely optical: last year Navratri ran 11 days against ten and coincided with the GST 2.0 rollout," said FADA president Sai Giridhar.Maruti Suzuki India, the largest carmaker, said Navratri deliveries were about 98% of last year, and it could have sold more with better supply. "Non-availability of vehicles is an issue. If I had more, we would have sold more. Every dealer is asking for more," said Partho Banerjee, senior executive officer-sales and marketing at Maruti. The company gets 12,000-12,500 bookings daily but can supply only 8,000-8,500. Pending bookings rose to 2.7 lakh after Dussehra from about 2 lakh at the start of October.Also Read: Carmakers gear up with multi-powertrain models as Indian buyers shift beyond petrol, dieselJATO Dynamics data shows registrations of petrol, diesel and CNG cars at the top makers fell 5.2% to 1.69 lakh units. Maruti registered 74,387 cars, up 0.1%. Tata Motors fell 16.4% to 24,843 units, Hyundai 2.7% to 19,706 and Kia 9.3% to 9,731, while Mahindra & Mahindra rose 6.6% to 20,681. It said electric car registrations also fell 5.1% to 11,478 units.Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles said demand remained strong. "The response during Navratri has been particularly encouraging, with over 50,000 vehicles delivered during this festive period, including more than 10,000 on Dussehra alone," said Amit Kamat, chief commercial officer, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles.Hyundai Motor India said registrations during Shradh and Navratri grew 30% to nearly 41,000 units. "Considering the pace of bookings, we expect momentum to continue through Dhanteras and Diwali," said chief executive officer Tarun Garg.Dealers said the real picture will emerge in a few days. "We will get to know the real picture after a few days as Vahan portal captures registration with a lag," said a dealer principal.

items.title: How the Mecca defense agreement works
items.summary: Ankara: Turkey's government has asked parliament to ratify a mutual defense agreement it signed with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, bringing the country closer to bolstering Saudi defenses as it faces attacks from Iran-backed Houthi rebels.Mirroring NATO's Article 5, the so-called Mecca Joint Defense Agreement commits the sides to view an armed attack against one as an attack on all three.While Turkey says that it's considering sending military support to Saudi Arabia, officials have cautioned that the pact is defensive in nature and that no Turkish troops will be deployed to fight in Yemen or attack the Houthis.Turkish and Pakistani officials have also insisted that the pact isn't against Iran or any other country, but haven't said how they would react if attacked by Iran.Regional countries take responsibility for their securityThe agreement was signed in the Saudi holy city of Mecca in August by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif with the aim of increasing cooperation and deterrence among the three regional heavyweights at a time of increased uncertainty amid the Iran war.It brings together oil-rich Saudi Arabia and nuclear power Pakistan as well as Turkey, which has NATO's second-largest army and a rapidly growing defense industry. It enables the three to take greater charge for their own security at a time of reduced U.S. involvement.For Pakistan, the Mecca Agreement builds on existing military ties with Riyadh. Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed a separate mutual defense agreement in September 2025.Pakistani Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar has repeatedly said that the Mecca agreement doesn't replace existing agreements and is open to other countries willing to uphold its principles and resolve differences peacefully.Nature of assistance planned is still unknownDuring an emergency meeting in Riyadh earlier this month, the three countries agreed to immediately implement what they said were their collective defense commitments, including arrangements for the rapid deployment of agreed upon military forces and capabilities to Saudi Arabia. They didn't elaborate.Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan has said that Turkey and Pakistan were assessing possible air defense, electronic warfare and technical assistance for Saudi Arabia."What type of assistance can be provided, especially in areas such as air defense and electronic warfare, what technical support can be offered? Work on these issues is ongoing," he said."Turkey will not be sending troops into another country's territory to carry out an attack. It is a defense agreement," Fidan said, addressing concerns raised by opposition parties that Turkey would be drawn into the conflict in Yemen.Authorities in Pakistan have declined to disclose deployment details, citing operational confidentiality. Officials say, however, that Pakistan's role would be strictly defensive. The Pakistani Information Ministry recently dismissed as "speculative" news reports that said Pakistan had already deployed between 30,000 and 40,000 troops to Saudi Arabia.Comment from Saudi Arabia on the pact since the Houthi attacks has been limited. In a post on X following a visit by Pakistan's army chief, Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman said: "We affirmed our commitment to continuing joint efforts to confront these attacks in accordance with the Mecca Agreement for Joint Defense."10-year commitment to the pactLittle was known about the content of the pact until Turkey's government submitted it to parliament for approval on Tuesday.The 16-article agreement, published by Turkish state broadcaster TRT on its website, states that the countries would defend each other militarily in case of external aggression in line with the U.N. Charter's right of self-defense.The agreement also paves the way for military cooperation, including joint training programs, exercises and personnel exchanges. It allows cooperation in the defense industry, including joint weapons production and technology transfers as well as intelligence sharing.A surprise clause states that the parties wouldn't be able to withdraw from the pact for 10 years, after which they would need to provide a three-month notice to leave.A parliamentary committee is expected to review the agreement in the coming days before it reaches the Turkish parliament's general assembly for ratification. Separately, Turkey's parliament would have to authorize any deployment of Turkish military personnel.Pakistan's potential contributionsPakistan hasn't sought parliamentary endorsement of the Mecca agreement, but officials say the government and other national institutions support it. They say Islamabad would provide whatever military assistance Saudi Arabia needs to defend the kingdom and Islam's holiest sites.Pakistan's military has more than two decades of experience fighting militant groups, which analysts say could help it bolster Saudi defenses.The agreement builds on decades of Pakistani military service in Saudi Arabia. An unspecified number of Pakistani troops have been stationed in Saudi Arabia since the early 1980s to train and advise Saudi forces.Pact to be led by retired Pakistani generalEven before the ratification process has been completed, the three countries established and convened a meeting of the so-called Strategic Political and Defense Committee composed of the foreign ministers, defense ministers and chiefs of staff.The committee is expected to meet twice a year.The pact's secretariat will be based in Saudi Arabia, and retired Pakistani Gen. Nauman Mahmood has been selected as its first secretary-general. He will serve a three-year term.

Recently, the World Bank raised India's GDP growth forecast for the current fiscal year to 7.1 per cent, up 0.5 percentage points from its April projections, supported by robust domestic demand and strong exports, despite global headwinds.

The Delhi Development Authority (DDA) may start its tethered hot air balloon rides from November 14, officials said on Wednesday.
The rides were launched last November from Baanseera park in Sarai Kale Khan area.
"We plan to start the rides from November 14 for the public, the weather is ideal for the launch of the rides and it will be in the same format like last year," a private organiser said.
Ticket prices are likely to be less than last year to attract more customers, he added.
The organisers set the ticket price at around Rs 2,300 per person last time.
DDA, last year, finalised the Yamuna Sports Complex, the Commonwealth Games sports complexes, and Asita and Baansera, two sites along the Yamuna Bank, for balloon rides.
Expansion plans, beyond Baanseera, are on hold.
A trip normally lasts between 7 and 12 minutes, with four people in the balloon.

items.title: Stephen Hubbard’s long road to release
items.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin announced the release of American citizen Stephen Hubbard on Wednesday, at the start of talks with US special envoy Steve Witkoff. The 74-year-old retired teacher had been serving a prison sentence in Russia after a court convicted him of being a mercenary in Ukraine.Hubbard's case drew attention because of his age, the circumstances surrounding his capture and conflicting accounts of his alleged involvement in the war.Who is Stephen Hubbard?Hubbard grew up in Big Rapids, Michigan, and served in the US Air Force and National Guard, according to military records cited by *The New York Times*.He later earned a master's degree in English and spent 25 years in Japan teaching the language. He subsequently moved to Cyprus before settling in Izyum, a city in eastern Ukraine, in 2014 with a Ukrainian partner, his sister Patricia Hubbard Fox told Reuters.Fox said in 2024 that her brother lived on a pension of around $300 a month and had limited contact with local residents. The siblings last spoke in September 2021.How was Hubbard captured?Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 and captured Izyum two months later. Ukrainian forces recaptured the city in September that year, but Hubbard was already in Russian custody.Russian state media reported that he had been detained in April 2022 and alleged that he was manning a Ukrainian military checkpoint. Reuters could not independently establish the circumstances of his capture.Fox said she recognised her brother in a YouTube video showing a man being questioned about his views on Putin and the war. A separate video appeared to show the man with his hands bound and being struck with a sandal. Reuters could not verify when or where the footage was recorded.Why was he imprisoned in Russia?In October 2024, a Moscow court convicted Hubbard of being a mercenary following a closed trial and sentenced him to six years and 10 months in prison.Prosecutors alleged that he had joined a Ukrainian territorial defence unit, received training, weapons and ammunition, and been promised a monthly payment of $1,000. Russian state media reported that he had pleaded guilty.His sister questioned that account, saying Hubbard held pro-Russian views and was unlikely to have taken up arms at his age.Martin De Luca, Hubbard's US-based lawyer, told Reuters in June 2025 that his client denied the allegations. According to De Luca, Hubbard said he had never belonged to a combat or military unit and that Russian soldiers had taken him from his home.What happened during his detention?The US State Department designated Hubbard as wrongfully detained in January 2025, allowing Washington to pursue efforts to secure his release. The department said Russia had denied US officials consular access to him.The New York Times reported in February 2025 that Hubbard had been transferred between at least five Russian detention centres before his trial.His legal team learnt only in April 2025 that he was being held at a facility in the Mordovia region, east of Moscow, De Luca said.Putin's announcement on Wednesday marks a significant development in Hubbard's case. Further details of the circumstances of his release were not immediately available in the information provided.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Adani Group chairman Gautam Adani and Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran in Mumbai on Wednesday morning before heading to Jamnagar in Gujarat to visit Reliance Industries' giant oil-refining complex, the world's largest single-site refinery, along with Vantara and giga factories being developed by the conglomerate.
Rubio, who arrived in Mumbai on Tuesday afternoon, first met Adani, followed by a meeting with Chandrasekaran, sources said.
Neither side released details of the meetings.
Adani heads one of India's largest conglomerates, with interests spanning ports, airports, energy, logistics and infrastructure. The group has also been expanding its renewable-energy and manufacturing businesses, sectors that are central to India's ambitions to strengthen domestic supply chains and attract global investment.
Chandrasekaran, who leads Tata Sons, the Tata Group's holding company, oversees a sprawling business empire with interests in automobiles, .

Poll interference is hard. Fooling voters is easy
items.summary: You’ve likely heard the ominous what-if scenarios about election disruptions in November: immigration agents or federal troops roaming polling places, federal officials seizing ballots and voting machines, and President Donald Trump issuing an executive order postponing or cancelling the election. Courts and legal experts have given solid reasons that each one of those potential election disruptions is unlikely. But the threats have served their purpose: People are harbouring doubts.The federal government doesn’t have to interfere with the mechanics of the voting process to disrupt the election. The easiest way for bad actors to interfere in the midterm elections right now is to let fear and distrust mess with our minds. By intimidating people into thinking they’ll face harassment at the polls or casting doubt on the integrity of the process, the administration is planting the seeds that the results can’t be trusted.I recently spoke with a naturalized US citizen from Venezuela who lives in Miami. She’s a young professional, married with kids, and until recently had been an active member of her local political party. She’s a reliable voter, but she told me she won’t be voting in person this year. The ICE raids that have terrorized her community have left her and her neighbors isolated and afraid.“I don’t want to go and vote in person, because I am terrified that they’re going to bring out the National Guard,” she told me. “You know, I have PTSD.”This is where Trump has brought us: US citizens fear risking their safety to exercise their constitutional right to vote.For the last 21 months, the federal government has mounted an unprecedented attack on state sovereignty over elections. Trump signed two executive orders that seek to radically dictate state election policy. The Department of Justice sued 30 states and the District of Columbia to gain access to sensitive voter data. The White House seized Georgia’s ballots from the 2020 election. And Trump tried to rehash his election conspiracy theories in a prime-time speech earlier this year.Judges from county courthouses to the US Supreme Court have rebuffed much of it. But the effort has undercut voter confidence. A University of Georgia survey of more than 11,000 voters found only 58% of Republicans, 63% of Democrats, and 49% of Independents trusted that votes would be counted accurately nationwide. And a recent poll from AP-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research found that only 34% of US adults trust government certifications of election results “a great deal” or “quite a bit,” down from 40% in 2024.Sometimes all it takes is a headline to sow doubt. That’s what happened in 2016 when Russian hackers got access to the Illinois state voter registration database. The hackers went unnoticed for weeks and only when they started accessing thousands of records per second did Illinois election officials shut the system down.“Russia wanted to be noticed,” said David Becker, who runs the non-partisan election watchdog site The Center for Election Innovation and Research. “They wanted the American people to think that our foreign adversaries had … the ability to change our elections.” Since then, US adversaries, particularly Russia, Iran and China, have focused on manipulating social media to make voters, particularly supporters of losing candidates, believe that their elections were stolen.Fortunately, millions of voters haven’t been intimidated by these global or domestic scare tactics. Records indicate that two weeks into early voting, an unprecedented number of votes have already been cast across the country, in many states exceeding records broken in 2018, 2022 and 2024.And in unprecedented fashion, state elections officials have locked arms in a bipartisan effort to resist any attempt by the administration to interfere.State officials are taking a traditional “all hazards approach,” said Minnesota Secretary of State Steve Simon, who leads the National Association of Secretaries of State. They’re prepared to handle election disruptions involving everything from natural disasters and bomb threats to power outages. This year, he told me, they’ve added “federal interference.”States have amassed teams of lawyers who are prepared to act quickly in the unlikely event that federal troops do show up, said Becker. They are also prepared to get before a judge if federal officials attempt to seize election equipment and get a ruling “before the chain of custody is irrevocably damaged,” he explained.But as a reminder, it’s a crime for anyone to order federal troops to a polling place — a violation punishable by up to five years in prison, a fine and disqualification from public office. Federal laws bar Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents from the polls. And it’s logistically impossible for Trump to cancel an election because thousands of officials across the country control elections, not the White House.The internet is an inviting host for allowing the mischief to continue in the weeks ahead. Let’s keep our wits about us. Thank the hard-working elections officials who keep the system sound, and don’t be duped.

US visa curbs not aimed at India: Rubio
items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has reiterated that the Trump's administration's ongoing clampdown on legal immigration is not a direct attack on India.In an interview with The Indian Express, Rubio said the changes were part of a broader effort to overhaul the US immigration system and are being applied globally.His comments came in response to a question about concerns among Indians, including students and the large diaspora in the US, over recent visa restrictions, the H-1B debate and a deepening anti-immigrant rhetoric. The question also referred to a recently foiled plot to attack a temple."So the first thing is that every country has to have immigration laws. If they don’t, they are not a sovereign country. And this is not about India; this applies globally," Rubio told The Indian Express.Rubio said that the US was dealing with the consequences of years of problems in its immigration system and argued that several immigration programmes had been abused. He also cited birth tourism as an example, saying it involved other countries rather than India."Frankly, we have seen many of these programmes being abused. Again, it is not unique to Indians or India," he said. "So we are trying to fix 20 years of neglect of an immigration system… and that is not targeted towards India," Rubio added.Why India feels the impactRubio acknowledged that changes to the US visa system can have a significant impact on Indians because of the large number of applicants from the country in some visa categories."Now, obviously, because of the developments, because of the ties between our countries, because of how developed your economy is, there are certain categories of visas that see a large number of Indians applying for," he said.The US, he said, still wants foreign students, workers, visitors and investors, but wants immigration to take place under laws that are followed."We want people to visit the United States. We want people to study in the United States. There are certain people that we want, that want to come work for a time in the United States. We want people to invest in the United States, and we are always going to have people immigrate to the United States," Rubio said."But we want it done through a system of laws that are complied with," he added.'Biggest threat to legal immigration is illegal immigration'Rubio also sought to draw a distinction between legal immigration and illegal immigration, arguing that large-scale unauthorised migration could undermine legal pathways."The biggest threat to legal immigration is illegal immigration. The biggest threat to legal immigration is mass migration, which again is not an Indian phenomenon (but) more unique to other parts of the world," he said.Rubio acknowledged that US policy changes could appear to be directed at India because of their effect on Indian applicants, but rejected that interpretation."And while I know that from your perspective here in India, it may seem targeted at India, (but) it’s not," he said."There is virtually no country on Earth that I visit where I don’t get a complaint about some visa or process, because we are fixing it globally."Rubio said the administration believed the changes would eventually make US immigration programmes more sustainable."Once it’s fixed, it will be far more sustainable. I actually think it will be better for the people using those programmes, and right and good for the United States," he said.
