The Paraguay international's shot revived memories of a strike from a similar range from David Beckham when playing for Manchester United against Wimbledon on the opening day of the 1996-97 Premier League season.

items.title: Fire at Canada military base kills 4
items.summary: Alberta: Four Canadian service members were killed and 39 people injured, including 19 critically, when a fast-moving fire overtook soldiers conducting live-fire combat training at a military base in Alberta, officials said Sunday.Maj. Gen. Wade Rutland said military officials knew about the fire for hours but believed it was sufficiently contained to allow training to continue before winds suddenly shifted, sending flames racing toward the soldiers."The fire was a kilometer away when the wind shifted. That is not normal for a fire to move a kilometer in 36 seconds," he said at a news conference in Edmonton.Rutland said a commander at the scene told him soldiers went from seeing no fire to having flames upon them in less than a minute.The fire broke out Saturday during high-intensity combat training involving Charlie Company of the 3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry.About 84 soldiers were split between a grenade range and an area where they practiced attacks on simulated enemy positions. The fire swept into the second training area.Rutland said investigators had not determined what ignited the grass fire.He said the battalion was preparing for rapid deployment to global crises and a mission to reinforce Canadian troops in Latvia next spring.The military identified those killed as Sgt. Morgan Wong of the Loyal Edmonton Regiment and Privates Shaun Farrell, Aidan Goulding and Hayden Lykkemark of the 3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry. All four were serving with the battalion, based in Edmonton.Alberta Premier Danielle Smith said 39 people were receiving medical care. Sayeh Zielke, chief executive of Acute Care Alberta, said 19 were in critical condition, eight were stable and 12 were ambulatory and receiving treatment for less serious injuries.Smith said some suffered severe burns and could face weeks or months of intensive treatment.Prime Minister Mark Carney described the incident as one of the worst peacetime tragedies for Canada's military on domestic soil. He ordered flags lowered to half-staff on federal buildings nationwide.Carney said the families of those killed had been notified. Those affected included regular forces personnel, reservists and soldiers from bases across Canada.Hospitals respond to mass casualtiesAlberta health officials said patients were transferred from Wainwright to four hospitals - the University of Alberta Hospital and Royal Alexandra Hospital in Edmonton, Foothills Medical Centre in Calgary and Red Deer Regional Hospital.Alberta officials said they had lifted the "Code Orange" emergency activated at several hospitals Saturday night to mobilize staff and beds for the casualties.The response involved 22 ground ambulances, six airplanes and two helicopters, with assistance from neighboring Saskatchewan. Smith said all patients had been accounted for and no further patients were awaiting transport.Wainwright Mayor Bruce Pugh said the town's small hospital was not designed to handle a mass-casualty incident but praised local medical personnel.Rutland confirmed that military search-and-rescue technicians parachuted into Wainwright to reinforce the emergency response. Pugh said their red parachutes were illuminated by flares as they descended shortly before midnight.Cathy Keane, a mayoral candidate in Ontario, said her eldest son was among those critically injured. "As a mother, right now I need to be with my son and family," she wrote on Facebook, saying she was traveling to Alberta.Conservative opposition leader Pierre Poilievre, who represents the area in Parliament, visited Wainwright on Sunday and said he had heard accounts of people who ran toward the danger to help others and were now fighting for their lives in hospitals.Military invest igates fireRutland said the fire ignited in the military training area, where multiple exercises were underway, and spread rapidly in unusually strong winds.He said winds had been within normal operating limits for much of Saturday, generally below 50 kph (31 mph), before intensifying rapidly. Range controllers rely on weather reports to determine whether training can safely continue, he said.The fire crossed established firebreaks before being contained with help from municipal firefighters.The Canadian military said there were no indications of terrorism.Rutland said military investigators would examine the circumstances, including whether safety protocols needed to change. "If our protocols need to change, then they'll be updated," he said.The military typically convenes a formal board of inquiry after such incidents, Rutland said, cautioning that determining what happened would take time.Rutland said Charlie Company had been withdrawn from the training area and the rest of the battalion suspended training Sunday.The Royal Canadian Mounted Police said officers were called shortly after 4 p.m. Saturday following reports of a fire in the base's training area.Large areas of Alberta were hit by a windstorm Saturday, with gusts up to 100 kph (62 mph). The winds toppled trees, sent signs flying and pushed flames beyond the base into surrounding rural areas.By late Saturday, the Municipal District of Wainwright said the fire was being held and that property and critical infrastructure were protected. No evacuation order was issued for residents.CFB Wainwright is one of Canada's busiest military training bases, where soldiers prepare for combat operations.The fire also disrupted advance voting ahead of Monday's referendum on whether Alberta should begin a process that could lead to independence from Canada. Elections Alberta said the Wainwright Communiplex advance polling location closed early Saturday and election materials were transported securely.

items.title: Ukraine fires over 1000 drones at Russia
items.summary: Ukrainian strikes set an oil export terminal and a depot ablaze in St. Petersburg on Sunday as Kyiv launched more than 1,000 drones at Russia in one of its largest aerial attacks of the war.The strikes came as tensions between Kyiv and Washington deepened, with U.S. President Donald Trump criticizing Kyiv's attacks on Russian oil infrastructure and the prospect of further U.S. sanctions against Moscow still uncertain.Also read: Trump claims 'great progress' in Russia-Ukraine negotiations; accuses Zelenskyy of not making better deal 2 years agoTrump said Sunday that he decided to hold off on implementing new sanctions on Russia because he doesn't "want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table."In a social media post, the U.S. president defended his Friday order to issue a waiver to prevent new sanctions from being placed on Moscow from bipartisan criticism that he was favoring Russian President Vladimir Putin's interests over those of Ukraine. Trump said he believed new sanctions would undermine negotiations to bring about a diplomatic end to the war in Ukraine."I can sign it later, or any time that I want!" Trump added of the sanctions.Trump also lashed out at Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who has been critical of Trump's recent outreach to Putin, for launching strikes on Russian energy infrastructure during the conflict, claiming Zelenskyy "doesn't want to end this war."Zelenskyy: Waiving sanctions strengthens RussiaSpeaking on NBC's "Meet the Press" earlier on Sunday, Zelenskyy said waiving sanctions against Russia would strengthen Putin's war effort. He also said U.S.-Ukraine intelligence sharing had resumed after being "blocked for some period of time."Zelenskyy said that while he trusted Trump, siding with Moscow would be a tragedy and a "historic mistake" for Washington."People want to forget what's going on. But we can't give this possibility to forget, or to change reality, or to change the truth," Zelenskyy said. "We can't compare me and Putin. He's (an) aggressor. He occupied us. He killed adults and children, his soldiers. He's a terrorist. And that's why I hope that President Trump will be very clear with this position."Later Sunday, Zelenskyy said on social media that he had spoken with U.S. presidential envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner about the results of an Oct. 9 meeting between U.S. and Ukrainian negotiating teams in Miami, as well as "next steps in diplomacy."Two killed as Russia and Ukraine trade blowsOne person was killed and five others were wounded in the St. Petersburg attack, which sparked fires at the Petersburg Oil Terminal and the city's Ruchi oil depot, local Gov. Alexander Beglov said. A logistics center belonging to Russian retailer Ozon and a data center operated by Russian tech giant VK were also targeted, the companies confirmed.Russia's Defense Ministry said Sunday that its forces had destroyed 1,015 Ukrainian drones over 15 Russian regions, the annexed Ukrainian peninsula of Crimea and the Black Sea.Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov told Russian state news agency Tass that Kyiv was "resisting" Moscow's invasion but could not "change the current course of events."Meanwhile, in Ukraine, a woman was killed and a 6-year-old girl was among at least two other people wounded in two Russian attacks on the southern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia, local officials said Sunday.Russia continues energy attacks, Kyiv saysTrump announced on Oct. 11 that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an "energy ceasefire" in the 4½-year-old war, but offered no details. Kyiv reported Russian attacks on energy sites continued after Trump's announcement, and on Thursday said it had resumed strikes on Russian oil facilities after a three-day pause.Zelenskyy wrote on X on Sunday that Russia had attacked Ukraine's energy, oil and gas sectors 76 times in the week since Trump's announcement. The Ukrainian government initially said it was observing the ceasefire.Also read: Trump's decision to waive Russian sanctions outrages Congress, but no quick counter seenEnergy facilities in four Ukrainian regions were struck overnight, leaving tens of thousands of families without power, he said, accusing Russia of trying to cause a blackout."America should see that Russia is not taking any reciprocal steps in response to sanctions relief or agreements. On the contrary, they take every signal of an opportunity to make money as proof that their bet on war is paying off and they can keep fighting," the Ukrainian president wrote.Ukraine apology to Lithuania over drone alertUkraine's Foreign Ministry apologized on Sunday after a drone entered Lithuania's airspace, prompting authorities to issue an air raid warning.Russian electronic warfare may have diverted the drone during a Ukrainian operation against legitimate military targets in Russia, ministry spokesperson Heorhii Tykhyi said in a statement.Lithuanian authorities urged residents in two northern counties along the Latvian border to take cover early Sunday because of a possible drone incursion, public broadcaster LRT reported.A drone entered the northern Pasvalys region and damaged a moving car, LRT said, citing Lithuania's National Crisis Management Center. No injuries were reported.

Mutual fund holdings of IT stocks sink to record low in September
items.summary: Mumbai: Indian mutual funds' exposure to Information Technology (IT) stocks fell to an all-time low in September as concerns over artificial intelligence (AI) disruption, weak global client spending and subdued growth prospects weighed on the sector. The decline has pushed frontline IT stocks such as Infosys and TCS, once among fund managers' biggest holdings, out of mutual funds' top holdings lists.IT stocks accounted for 5.3% of mutual funds' equity assets under management (AUM) in September, compared with 7.6% at the end of 2025 and 9.24% at the end of 2024. The sector's weight had touched a record 13.4% at the end of 2021."The correction in Information Technology stocks during 2026 has been a de-rating story more than an earnings story," said Harsh Thakkar, equity research analyst at Samco Securities.135037302The value of mutual funds' IT holdings fell 25% to ₹2.97 lakh crore in September from ₹3.98 lakh crore in December 2025, according to Prime Database. The value had reached a record ₹4.03 lakh crore in November 2025.Infosys, which was among the five largest holdings of mutual funds at the start of 2026, slipped to 10th place in September. TCS has seen a similar decline. The stock, which ranked 10th among mutual fund holdings in 2024 and was among the top 14 in 2025, slipped to 18th place in September.HCL Tech and Tech Mahindra, which ranked 20th and 25th among mutual funds' largest holdings at the beginning of 2026, slipped to 25th and 31st positions, respectively, in September. Wipro fell sharply to 316th place from 88th at the start of 2026 and 56th in 2024.Read more: Mega Jio Platforms IPO to lead Rs 31,663 crore offerings this week; 9 listings lined upMany fund managers have cut their exposure due to uncertainty over the extent of disruption that AI could bring into the software services industry."Revenue growth has remained muted but has not collapsed," said Thakkar. "However, valuations have fallen sharply because investors priced in the potential threat from AI agents to the labour-intensive application development and maintenance business model."Read more: Can Nifty, Sensex rally further or will bears reign in? 5 factors to steer market this weekWeighed down by these concerns, the Nifty IT index till October 8 had shed about 28% in 2026 as against the 14% decline in the Nifty. But, a rebound since then has helped cut losses, with the index running up 11.7% last week, posting its biggest weekly gains in 18 years, amid a sharp sell-off in AI-related semiconductor stocks elsewhere in Asia on concerns over the durability of their recent rally."Promising management commentary, the anti-AI trade turning favourable for Indian IT companies and valuations that are very reasonable at the moment, below their five-year average and closer to the 10-year average," said Kunal Bajaj, research analyst at Choice Institutional Equities.While the industry cut its exposure to IT stocks, fund houses also made some additions to their holdings. In Infosys, funds increased their holdings by 2.7 crore shares to 86 crore shares in September from 83.4 crore shares in December 2025. In TCS, they added 61 lakh shares, taking their holdings to 20.64 crore shares from around 20 crore.Mutual funds also increased their holdings in HCL Tech by 1.8 crore shares to 26.4 crore from 24.6 crore. But, they reduced their holdings in Tech Mahindra by 45 lakh shares to 18.97 crore from 19.42 crore.In Wipro, their holdings fell by 33.96 crore shares to 17.42 crore from 51.39 crore at the beginning of year.

Exporters may have to track emissions
items.summary: New Delhi: The government has begun discussions on whether Indian exporters should track indirect emissions across their supply chains as trade partners tighten green requirements and global value chains become increasingly interconnected.The finance and commerce & industry ministries have held preliminary discussions on whether Scope 3 emissions should be measured for exports to all countries, rather than only for markets such as the European Union and the UK, which have introduced Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) measures.Scope 3 emissions cover indirect emissions across a company's value chain, including those linked to purchased goods and services, capital goods, transportation, waste, business travel, employee commuting, leased assets, raw material extraction and the sourcing of imported raw materials. Measuring them is more complex than tracking emissions directly generated by a company or those associated with the energy it purchases.Also Read | Faster services imports threaten to erode cushion against India’s goods trade deficit: Report"There is one thought that measurement of Scope 3 emissions can't be done for the EU alone. It would have to do for all countries because the value chains are linked," said an official, adding that the indirect nature of these emissions makes them particularly challenging to measure, report and mitigate. However, no decision has been taken on the issue.Niti Aayog, in its report titled Scenarios Towards Viksit Bharat And Net Zero: Financing Needs, has said that any inclusion of Scope 3 disclosures should be phased and proportionate, beginning with large entities in high-impact sectors to avoid imposing disproportionate compliance burdens on micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and smaller suppliers.135034854The existing CBAM frameworks provide for the determination of direct and indirect greenhouse gas emissions covered under Scopes 1 and 2 of the Greenhouse Gas Protocol. Indian exporters of iron and steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, electricity and hydrogen products are already subject to the EU's CBAM.Also Read | What is holding up the US-India trade deal?"The CBAM is already a challenge for us because we don't have basic data on our raw material emissions. Disclosures on Scope 2 are posing a problem, so adding Scope 3 emissions data on what is my electricity provider and transportation would be unviable," said a steel exporter to the EU. Under the EU CBAM, the central platform will open for the sale of CBAM certificates on February 1, 2027. Importers must submit their first annual CBAM declaration and surrender certificates covering all 2026 imports by September 30, 2027.

items.title: Europe refused China, India oil sanctions
items.summary: Washington, Amid intense criticism, the US on Sunday said the waiver of sanctions on Russia and tariffs on other countries, including India, was a 60-day pause to analyse the global impact of the measure.Trump's cabinet colleagues Marco Rubio and Scott Bessent said the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act granted the President the flexibility to assess the situation."No sanctions were lifted on Friday," Bessent told NBC's Meet the Press, referring to the Executive Order signed by Trump granting a waiver from sanctions under the Graham Act passed with overwhelming bipartisan support last month.Bessent revealed that the US had asked its European allies to impose secondary sanctions on China and India for buying Russian oil, but they refused."So why should the US bear the burden? President Trump, perhaps we will be in contact with our European partners. Why should the US go it alone," Bessent said, adding that European countries had waived an embargo on purchase of Russian diesel and jet fuel in May.On Saturday evening, Secretary of State Rubio said waivers were included in the Graham Act to study the different things going around the world, such as the pressure on global energy supplies due to the Iran war, the attack of Houthis in Saudi Arabia and the Ukraine-Russia war."I think the president wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyse what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy, and even to the US economy," Rubio told reporters before leaving on a six-day visit to Uzbekistan and India.The executive order signed by Trump on Friday states that the waivers shall remain in effect until such time as the President or the Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury and the Trade Representative, as appropriate, determine that further action is appropriate.Speaking to reporters at Mar-a-Lago resort near Miami on Saturday, Trump said his decision to waive sanctions under the Graham Act would benefit the US."A lot of you don't know what my decision is yet, but we'll figure it out, and you'll figure it out,"  he said."It's a very good decision, and it's going to be a decision that's good for the country, and I think good for the world because we're really at a world stage,"  Trump said.Bessent also accused the European nations of fuelling Russia's war on Ukraine by buying oil and gas from Moscow."The Europeans have given Russia and Vladimir Putin more money than they've given the Ukrainians. They continue to gorge on Russian energy," Bessent said."The Europeans are financing the Russian war machine. The US imports USD four billion of Russian products. USD 1.8 billion of that is fertiliser. The Europeans import more than 10 times that," Bessent said.Trump's decision to waive sanctions on Russia came under fire from the Republicans and Democrats, who last month came together to overwhelmingly pass the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act.Senator Darline Graham, a Republican from South Carolina, also criticised Trump for exempting Russia from a sanctions law that was championed by and named after her late brother Lindsey.Indian-American lawmakers, most of whom had voted against the Graham Act, were sharply critical of Trump's decision."Trump's decision to waive new sanctions on Russia should leave no doubt: that is exactly what is happening," Congressman Ami Bera said on X."My Republican colleagues pushed hard to pass the Lindsey Graham Russia sanctions bill before we left town. They ought to be standing up and screaming at the top of their lungs that we don't side with Russia," he said."Trump is doing exactly what we warned: undermining Congress' authority, abandoning Ukraine, and letting Putin off the hook," Congressman Suhas Subramanyam said on X."Republicans refused to let us vote on stronger Russia sanctions. Now we - and our allies - are paying the price," Subramanyam said.

This was followed by Kathivakkam.The Greater Chennai Corporation said that pro-active field operations, constant rescue efforts and continued coordination made sure that major areas and subways did not face waterlogging amid severe weather conditions.A team from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and four teams from the Tamil Nadu Disaster Response Force (TNDRF) were deployed on the ground to handle vulnerable areas. Nine relief centres were established, and food was being steadily distributed to residents.Also Read: India faces weakest monsoon in nearly two decades as El Nino strengthensRainwater has now been completely cleared from all major bus routes and streets. Pumping operations in remaining low-lying pockets were in final stages and would end shortly, thereby keeping the entire situation under control.Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay and Minister for Public Works and Youth Welfare and Sports Development, Aadhav Arjuna, visited the Ripon Building, GCC headquarters, following heavy rainfall across the city and red alert.During his visit, Aadhav Arjuna met teams from NDRF and TNDRF deployed for rescue operations, held consultations, and issued necessary directives regarding rescue and relief measures.

CISF to roll out reorganisation from Nov 1
items.summary: In a historic step, the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) will implement a major functional reorganisation of its administrative and operational structure from November 1 to strengthen specialised security management across critical infrastructure and strategic establishments nationwide.The reorganisation, approved by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), will realign the force's existing territorial sectors according to the specific security requirements of different industries and establishments, including power, coal, steel, petroleum and natural gas, ports, government buildings, museums, monuments and mass rapid transit systems.Under the revised structure, the force said, the National Capital Region Sector will be reorganised as the Government Building Museums and Monuments and Mass Rapid Transit System (GBMM & MRTS) Sector, New Delhi.The North Sector in New Delhi and North Eastern Sector-II in Kolkata will be restructured as the Power-I and Power-II Sectors, respectively. The Eastern Sector in Ranchi will become the Coal Sector, while the Central Sector in Bhilai will be converted into the Steel Sector.Similarly, the North Eastern Sector in Guwahati will become the Petroleum and Natural Gas Sector. The Western Sector in Mumbai and the South Sector in Chennai will be transformed into the West Coast Port Sector and East Coast Port Sector, respectively.The existing Department of Atomic Energy and Department of Space (DAE & DoS) Sector in Bengaluru, Airport Sector-I in New Delhi and Airport Sector-II in Bengaluru will continue under their respective functional arrangements.The reorganisation, it said, aims to improve operational oversight, develop sector-specific expertise, ensure greater uniformity in security practices and strengthen coordination with the concerned ministries, departments and installation managements.The CISF provides security to a wide range of establishments, including airports, seaports, atomic energy and space installations, power plants, power grids, steel plants, coal mines, petroleum and natural gas facilities, currency note presses, government buildings, iconic monuments and mass transit systems.Each sector has distinct operational processes, infrastructure, potential hazards and security vulnerabilities, requiring specialised security arrangements.Under the earlier system, administrative and operational supervision was largely organised on the basis of territorial jurisdiction. Over the past 25 years, the force has progressively adopted a functional approach in selected sectors, including aviation and strategic establishments under the Department of Atomic Energy and the Department of Space.The experience gained from this approach highlighted the advantages of specialised supervision, focused training, sector-specific Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), better utilisation of specialised personnel and closer coordination with the concerned organisations.Building on this experience, the CISF reviewed the supervisory structure of the remaining territorial sectors and undertook the functional realignment following deliberations with supervisory formations, branches at force headquarters and senior officers, before obtaining MHA approval.The restructuring assumes significance as the CISF's mandate is expanding beyond conventional industrial security to cover new and specialised responsibilities.The force has been designated as a Recognised Security Organisation (RSO) for port facilities under the International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code. The functional realignment of port-sector supervision is expected to support specialised port-security expertise and improve coordination with port authorities and other stakeholders.The CISF has also been entrusted with security responsibilities at high-security correctional facilities in Jammu and Kashmir and designated as the nodal agency for aerial security of critical infrastructure.The force is strengthening its cybersecurity and drone and anti-drone capabilities through specialised training and collaboration with premier institutions to improve preparedness against cyberattacks, digital threats and hostile unmanned aerial systems.The reorganisation is expected to establish a more specialised, sector-oriented security apparatus, improve operational accountability and strengthen protection of India's strategic and economic assets.

The Genius HRTech report is based on inputs from 1,255 employees during September 1-30 across sectors, including Information Technology (IT), manufacturing, telecom, retail, finance and BFSI, FMCG and engineering, among others.

items.title: Trivandrum airport halts flights on Tue
items.summary: Flight operations at Thiruvananthapuram International Airport will be suspended for five hours on October 20 to allow the traditional Arattu procession of Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple to pass across the runway.Thiruvananthapuram International Airport Ltd (TIAL) said on Sunday that flight services would remain suspended from 4 pm to 9 pm to facilitate the temple’s ‘Alpassi Arattu’ procession. Passengers have been advised to check revised flight timings with their respective airlines.Also read: Vietnam Airlines set to fly non-stop between Hanoi and Ahmedabad from November 2026The temporary suspension is part of a centuries-old tradition associated with the Travancore royal family. The procession takes the ceremonial idols of the temple to Shangumugham beach for a ritual holy bath before returning to the shrine.The airport has adjusted its operations twice a year for decades to accommodate the temple’s biannual Arattu processions. The practice continues despite the growth of the airport and changes in its management.The tradition dates back to the period of the erstwhile Travancore kingdom and has continued since the airport was established in 1932.Also read: Indian passport rises to 84th rank in Henley Passport Index 2026; visa-free access to 55 destinationsAccording to historians, the then Travancore king, Sree Chithira Thirunal, had stipulated that the airport would remain open to the public for 363 days a year, with the remaining two days reserved for Lord Padmanabha, the titular deity of the royal family.The ritual has continued even after the Adani Group took over the airport’s management. The runway crossing is a distinctive feature of the ceremony, reflecting the historical relationship between the temple, the former royal family and the airport. The temporary closure requires airlines to adjust their schedules to accommodate the procession.Passengers travelling to or from Thiruvananthapuram on October 20 should check with their airlines for updated departure and arrival times before heading to the airport.

The restriction, initially imposed on April 23, 2025, has been extended periodically since then amid strained relations between the two neighbouring countries.
The Pakistan Airports Authority (PAA) announced the extension in a post on X on Saturday, saying the restriction also covers military flights.
The latest extension will remain in effect until 4:59 am (local time) on November 24, 2026, according to the authority.

items.title: Tata Trusts disbursed ₹1,556 crore in FY26, plans 40-50 nonprofit hospitals
items.summary:
Tata Trusts, India's largest philanthropic group, disbursed Rs 1,556.31 crore in the year to March 2026 and is now working toward a network of 40 to 50 not-for-profit general hospitals, Chairman Noel Tata said in the Trusts' Annual Report for 2025-26.
Tata said patients who can afford to pay would help fund care for those who cannot. The report gives no investment figure, locations, or timeline for the hospitals.
In his message, Tata said the Trusts want to build institutions and models that become "enduring public assets" and be judged on what changes as a result of their work. He wrote that measuring philanthropy by people reached or money spent is no longer enough.
Institutional grants and direct project spending came in at Rs 1,353.32 crore, and individual grants at  Rs 202.99 crore. Rural upliftment took the largest share at Rs 457.62 crore, followed by education (Rs 270.26 crore), cancer care (Rs 178.46 crore), institutions (Rs 169.31 crore) and healthcare (Rs 105.97 crore). .

items.summary:
Japan is set to launch a spacecraft on the world's first mission to bring back samples from Phobos, one of the two small, potato-shaped moons orbiting Mars.
Scientists hope the mission, which is expected to take five years, will provide clues to how Phobos and its smaller sibling Deimos formed, and hopefully even shed light on the origins of life in the solar system.
The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency's launch of the spacecraft Tuesday on a new Japanese mainstay H-3 rocket comes as the United States, China and others consider sending astronauts to Mars.
Samples from Phobos will provide useful data for scientists to consider using a Martian moon as a base for a future manned mission to the planet, said MMX project manager Yasuhiro Kawakatsu.
"Despite their potential importance, Martian moons have never been fully investigated," Kawakatsu said. "They are known as the most important unclimbed mountains in the solar system."

Rioters clashed with police, looted stores and set property on fire in central Milan on Saturday, emptying Piazza del Duomo and a luxury shopping arcade when the area would usually be teeming with shoppers.
The march against wars and rising living costs began peacefully. But masked protesters threw stones, paving blocks and other objects at riot police and set fire to barricades made from bar tables. Images of the aftermath showed a severely damaged carabinieri car.
Police used water cannons and tear gas to disperse the crowds.
At least two police officers were injured and about 50 demonstrators, including many minors, were detained, the LaPresse news agency reported.
Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni condemned the violence in a social media post.
"Demonstrating is a right. Setting our cities ablaze is not," she wrote, citing "hooligans who exploit demonstrations to sow chaos, attack those responsible for ensuring security and hold entire cities hostage".

items.summary:
Pope Leo returned to the Vatican on Saturday, four days after undergoing surgery for lung cancer at Rome's Gemelli Hospital, where dozens of well-wishers saw him off with cries of "Holiness."
"I am better, thank you," the pope said when asked how he was as he was driven away in a black SUV.

items.title: More US universities to face J-1 visa probes
items.summary: More US universities could come under investigation for potential J-1 visa fraud, US Department of Labor Inspector General Anthony D'Esposito said. He also said that subpoenas had been served and investigations were already underway.“Nine universities under investigation for potential J-1 visa fraud—more to come. Companies suspended. Warrants executed. Subpoenas issued. American first. Just getting started," D'Esposito said in a post on X.— USLaborIG (@USLaborIG) Earlier, last Thursday, US Vice President JD Vance announced a federal investigation into nine universities over their use of J-1 visas. He alleged that some institutions were bringing foreign researchers to the US at lower wages than those paid to American workers.Also Read: US announces investigation into 9 universities, including Ivy League schools, over J-1 visasThe universities named in the investigation are the University of Pittsburgh, Yale University, Harvard University, Stanford University, Brown University, the University of California, Davis, the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), Arizona State University and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT).Vance alleged that American graduate students and researchers earned about $20,000 more than foreign researchers brought in under the J-1 programme for comparable work. He also said foreign nationals accounted for about 61% of postdoctoral workers and researchers supported by federal grants at the nine universities, compared with 38% at other universities.Also Read: US universities review CPT rules for international students as higher education groups seek court relief, hearing on November 6The J-1 visa programme allows foreign nationals to enter the US temporarily as exchange visitors for activities such as research, teaching, internships, training and other educational or cultural exchanges.The Labor Department's inspector general has also announced a Visa Fraud Strike Team to investigate and prosecute suspected visa fraud in high-risk programmes, including J-1 and H-1B visas. The initiative will bring together personnel from the departments of Labor, Justice and Homeland Security, US Citizenship and Immigration Services, Homeland Security Investigations and the State Department's Diplomatic Security Service.The authorities have said the investigation will examine whether visa misuse, improper financial relationships or foreign influence are compromising federally funded research.

items.title: Gujarat chemical plant blast kills 5, injures 5 in Bharuch district

The blast occurred around 10 pm on Friday during a hydrogenation process at SynZeal Pharmachem in the Saykha GIDC area in Vagra taluka, triggering a toxic leak of methylene dichloride (MDC) gas, they said.

items.title: US to revive 3 shuttered nuclear plants to meet rising electricity demand
items.summary:
The United States is making an unprecedented attempt to revive three shuttered nuclear plants to meet rising energy demand, including from large-scale data centres.
No commercial nuclear reactor is known to have resumed generating electricity after beginning the decommissioning process that takes one out of service, though some reactors have restarted after long outages.
The Department of Energy is lending as much as USD 4.4 billion to restart the Palisades Power Plant in Michigan, the Crane Clean Energy Centre on Pennsylvania's Three Mile Island and the Duane Arnold Energy Centre in Iowa to restore a combined 2.25 gigawatts of electricity, which can power roughly 2 million homes and businesses. All three of the plants closed before their licenses expired, largely because the electricity they produced was considered too expensive.
Not anymore. Two of the plants have contracts with Big Tech companies that will pay a premium to get large amounts of carbon-free energy for data centres.

items.title: Yemen officials blame Houthis for 2 missile strikes on Yemen's Aden airport

Two missiles struck the airport in Yemen's port city of Aden on Friday night, police said, blaming Iran-backed Houthi rebels for the second such attack in less than a week.
Police said no casualties were reported as fighting escalates in the latest front in the Iran war, one in which the rebels have attacked both neighbouring Saudi Arabia and Yemen's internationally recognized government that's backed by the kingdom.
A security official and a traffic controller said an area of the Aden airport that hosts a military unit aligned with the Saudi-backed government was hit. Both spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to the media.
There was no immediate claim of responsibility.
The attack came a day after the Houthis carried out a deadly strike on a palace complex in Aden, which has been the seat of the internationally recognized government since 2015.

The development comes amid complaints that the names of many living voters and those who were living at their registered address were also removed from the draft rolls published on August 31.
Kumar said that around 25 lakh cases out of 33.12 lakh, in which voters who were issued notices for non-mapping or logical discrepancy, have also been resolved.

items.title: Tennis player Stefan Milicevic handed 24-year suspension for match-fixing
items.summary:
- Serbian tennis player Stefan Milicevic has been given a 24-year ban for allegedly fixing multiple matches and recruiting other players into a "corrupt network," the International Tennis Integrity Agency said Thursday.
The agency said the 29-year-old Milicevic was charged with fixing six matches - including five of his own - and trying to fix six more between 2022 and 2024. He is banned from tennis until 2050.
Milicevic never reached a singles ranking higher than 1,338 and only played in lower-tier events. But the ITIA also charged him with recruiting "multiple professional players as part of a corrupt network" that resulted in "a number of other players fixing matches" during those same years.
The agency did not give details about which matches were fixed, or name any of the other players involved.
It said Milicevic did not cooperate into its investigation into the fixed matches and did not respond to its findings. It also fined Milicevic $70,000.

The Fed increased its key interest rate by a quarter-point to about 3.9 per cent in September, its first increase in three years, and stubbornly elevated US inflation will likely lead it to hike that rate again in coming months to slow spending and help cool price pressures.
But Warsh offered no fresh signals during a "fireside chat" with International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva at a meeting of financial leaders in Bangkok.

However, geopolitical tensions, volatile energy prices and trade disruptions pose risks to the growth outlook, it added.
Deloitte India Economist Rumki Majumdar said over the past decade, India's growth has rested on resilient household spending and sustained investment push in public infrastructure. Businesses now have better connectivity, healthier balance sheets, and higher capacity utilisation, which strengthens the case for expansion.
"The question is whether these conditions will encourage private investment to play a larger role in boosting growth in the coming years. Recent indicators offer grounds for optimism. items.title: Anti-India hate turning into violence: US lawmakers on temple shooting plot
items.summary:
A large number of US lawmakers and advocacy groups expressed shock at the alleged mass shooting attempt at a Hindu temple in Illinois, saying anti-India hatred was turning into violence.
A 19-year-old was arrested in Palatine near Chicago for planning a mass shooting at the Sri Venkateswara Temple in Aurora, Illinois on Sunday. The plan failed as the gun carried by the teenager jammed and could not fire.

items.title: Indian rice cooks up a 1-year price high
items.summary: Asian rice export prices in key hubs remained firm this week, with Indian rates hitting a more than one-year high on stronger rupee and crop supply concerns, while Vietnamese prices rose to a near two-month high on expectations of stronger demand.India's 5% broken parboiled variety  was quoted at $384-$389 per ton this week, up from last week's $378-$384. Indian 5% broken white rice was priced at $385 to $390 per ton."Paddy prices remain firm in the domestic market due to limited supplies. Production has declined in several states because of below-normal rainfall," said a Mumbai-based exporter.Vietnam's 5% broken rice  was offered at $440-$450 per metric ton on Thursday, its highest level since August 21, up from $420-$430 a week ago."We are told that the Philippines will resume rice purchases from Vietnam from November," a trader based in Ho Chi Minh City said.A Vietnamese agriculture ministry official said this week that rice export activity is expected to be busy during the rest of this year, adding that the country's target to export 8 million tons of rice will be met.In Thailand, 5% broken rice  was quoted at $480 per ton, highest since September 10, up from $465 to $468 last week.The arrival of vessels to collect rice shipments and additional purchases by some exporters pushed prices higher, a Bangkok-based rice trader said.Flooding has delayed loading, while some exporters have had to buy additional rice as the off-season harvest nears its end, adding upward pressure on prices, the trader said.Thailand's rice exports could fall short of this year's 7-million-ton target amid competition from India and Pakistan and weaker demand from major buyers, according to the Thai Rice Exporters Association.In Bangladesh, rice prices rose over the past week, driven by higher fuel costs and rising paddy prices, with fine rice rising to 74-75 taka per kilogram from 72 taka a week earlier, adding to the financial strain on consumers already grappling with persistently high living costs.($1 = 122.4000 taka)

Stock movements varied among leading companies as interest rates influenced market dynamics.

items.title: Demand for bank loans rises amid hardening yields
items.summary: Canara Bank and Indian Bank reported a total corporate loan pipeline of ₹1.10 lakh crore between them. The banks are experiencing steady credit demand from corporate clients amid rising bond yields. Canara Bank expects to maintain around 19% credit growth, while Indian Bank targets a 14-15% growth rate. Both banks highlighted the importance of improving deposit growth to narrow the credit-deposit gap.

SC ruling deals a heavy blow to Yes Bank's risk equity capital
items.summary: Yes Bank is facing a significant reduction in its Common Equity Tier-1 capital buffer following a recent Supreme Court ruling. The court reversed the earlier write-down of over $800 million related to additional Tier-1 bonds. Analysts suggest that this verdict could lower Yes Bank's CET1 ratio to approximately 11-11.5%. The bank is currently analyzing the judgment to assess the final impacts on its financial standing.

items.title: Homegrown firms enter budget smartphone market as memory chip prices rise
items.summary: India's budget smartphone market is opening up for local brands as global companies reduce their presence. Rising memory chip prices have significantly impacted entry-level smartphone production costs. Homegrown companies Ai+ and Lava are gaining traction in this competitive segment. Micromax plans to re-enter the smartphone market by evaluating various strategies. Brands aim to leverage the government's financial incentives under the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme to succeed.

items.title: DoT mandates telecom operators to display KYC-registered names for incoming calls starting November 1
items.summary: The Department of Telecommunications mandates telecom operators to show KYC-registered names with incoming calls from November 1. This initiative aims to reduce cyber fraud, phishing, and unwanted commercial calls. The amendment to Caller Line Identification will officially include Caller Name Identification for subscriber convenience. Trials and consultations informed the decision, involving both operators and civil society groups.

items.title: Robust pipeline: Hotel chains look beyond metros for growth
items.summary: India's hospitality sector is set to add 161,074 branded hotel rooms over the next five years. Approximately 117,000 of these rooms are currently in active development across various locations. Notably, four in five new rooms will be situated outside major hospitality markets, including tier-2 and tier-3 sites. In FY26, the industry reported steady occupancy rates and increases in average daily rates.

items.summary: Car sales in India saw a 22% increase in September due to dealers stocking up for festivals and strong demand. Two-wheelers and three-wheelers also experienced growth of 13.5% and 16% respectively during the same month. The overall sales for passenger vehicles increased by 28.3% in the first half of FY27. Automakers remain hopeful about continuous demand amidst ongoing geopolitical challenges.

items.title: Green Card lottery entries to reopen Nov 1
items.summary: A US federal judge has ordered the Trump administration to reopen registration for the 2027 Diversity Visa lottery, also known as the Green Card lottery, with the entry window set to open by November 1, 2026.The ruling restores a route to US permanent residency for eligible applicants after the government failed to start registration on time, according to Courthouse News Service report.Also Read: US judge blocks Trump policy of fining migrants up to $1.8 millionUS District Judge Jinsook Ohta issued the order on October 14, directing Secretary of State Marco Rubio and the US State Department to announce the registration dates and open the entry process for 30 days.The State Department must also accept eligible entries, notify selected applicants and process their cases under the programme's rules, the report said. A subsequent extension moved the registration deadline to November 1 and the deadline to notify selected applicants to December 3.Also Read: US raises select immigration fees for FY 2027, new charges from October 16Earlier in November 2025, the State Department had announced that it was making changes to the entry process for the 2027 lottery and would announce the registration dates later. The registration delay prompted California-based immigration law firm Red Eagle Law to file a lawsuit against the State Department. The firm argued that the government's failure to open registration had effectively cancelled the annual programme.The Diversity Visa programme offers up to 55,000 immigrant visas each year to eligible applicants from countries with historically low rates of immigration to the US.Applicants selected through the lottery must also meet eligibility requirements and complete the visa process as the selection in itself does not guarantee a Green Card.The 2027 programme's visa year ends on September 30, 2027. This means that applicants have limited time period to complete the required steps.

items.title: India-US trade deal: 'Big items done', both sides close to pact, says Gor
items.summary:
US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor on Thursday said negotiations for a bilateral trade deal were moving at an "incredible pace", and the "big items are done", underlining that he was confident that both sides will get the pact through.
During an interactive session at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum here, Gor also echoed External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar's assessment of the progress in the proposed India-US trade pact, saying "we are very close to landing it".
Asked about the status of the negotiations, Gor said, "I won't like to get into too many details at this stage, and let the ministers announce that. But in the grand scheme of things, big items are done."
"We're actively engaged... Within three weeks of arriving here, we announced a trade deal. The European Union trade deal took almost 20 years. So we're at an incredible pace, and I am confident that we will get it done," Gor said.

items.title: Govt revises windfall gains tax for petrol and diesel exports
items.summary: The central government has increased the windfall tax on petrol exports to Rs 2.5 per litre. Simultaneously, the windfall tax on diesel has been reduced to Rs 8.5 per litre. These adjustments will be effective from October 16, as announced by the central board of indirect taxes and customs.
